entries.subject: LAM/SPHERE MPCD: selected reconstruction
entries.finding: The current LAM 3Dshape directory lists 128_Nemesis_mpcd.obj, matching the actual preparation input. The retained measurements describe 2738 vertices and 5472 facets in km; the recipe preserves that source scale. This review checked the release listing and local source/recipe binding, not a fresh mesh reconstruction or new source-fit test.

entries.subject: Size and pole
entries.finding: The retained Table 1 and Table A.1 extract records diameter 163 km, ecliptic J2000 pole (313°, -19°), period 38.9325 h. Published survey diameter averages ADAM and MPCD; the released MPCD coordinates are not rescaled to that average. The measured source volume-equivalent radius is 83.00209257577323 km. These source interpretations were checked against the recipe; the paper table was not freshly re-transcribed in this pass.

entries.subject: Released SPHERE observations and surface registration
entries.finding: The live source folder https://observations.lam.fr/astero/Data/128Nemesis/ contains Deconv/ and Red/. Reduced and deconvolved observations therefore have a concrete archive route. Their pixels, image geometry, coverage and photometry were not qualified in this directory-level check, so these files cannot yet be treated as a registered global reflectance map. The current grid remains an explicit missing-imagery presentation.
entries.revisitWhen: The original image headers and publication establish a usable projection onto this specific MPCD model, and a native-pixel comparison qualifies geometry, illumination and measured coverage.

entries.subject: Released ADAM companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 128_Nemesis_adam.obj. The body’s retained model comparison already distinguishes this ADAM reconstruction from the selected MPCD mesh. It is not adopted as a duplicate view of the same measured shape; the original comparison remains linked.
entries.revisitWhen: An observation or scientific comparison specifically requires this alternative mesh and its matching source frame.

entries.subject: Released SAGE companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 128_Nemesis_sage.obj, which the imported ledger omitted. Its existence establishes a numerical candidate; method, calibration and independence from the selected MPCD reconstruction still need comparison.
entries.revisitWhen: The SAGE companion’s paper, scale and shape constraints have been compared with the selected MPCD release.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured on all 25 deconvolved frames with the release's rotation record, cast onto the released ADAM mesh: not one frame scores. The projected outline is round at every rotational phase, elongation 1.09 against the rule's 1.20 threshold, so the outline cannot define a position angle and the route has nothing to place this body with. Its record also states a period of 77.86 h where the survey publishes 38.93, exactly twice, which is a separate question but does not affect a round outline. Measured outside preparation by the registration stage's own modules (its limb fit, camera and caliper rule) driven from the pinned inputs, which reproduces Sylvia's prepared report to the digit (15 scored, rms 2.887, floor 1.871, systematic 2.198); on Themis it read 2.92 degrees where the stage itself read 1.65, so treat these as the rule applied to the frames, not as a prepared verdict.
entries.revisitWhen: A registration reference independent of this body's outline: a spacecraft map, or frames resolving surface markings.
